2. The brief facts of the plaintiff's case is as under :-
The plaintiff is the Proprietor of M/s. Bengal Sweets and it is running its business in the suit schedule property from past 31 years by obtaining registration certificate from the Department of Labour and the same is valid till 31.12.2023.
The plaintiff also obtained trade license from the Health Department and also obtained the license under Food and Safety Standards Authority of India.

sentences.text: The defendant No.1 in the month of May 2021 approached the plaintiff claiming to be President of Dalitha Yuvakara Sevadala and demanded sum of Rs 10,00,000/- to permit the plaintiff to continue running the business.
The plaintiff stated that he is running the business in compliance of all local laws and did not find a reason to pay the ransom as demanded by the Defendant No.1.
The plaintiff stated that the defendant No.1 again sent Defendants 2 to 4 to the shop on 16.11.2021 holding out a threat that they would shut the shop unless he pays a sum of Rs 10,00,000/-.
The defendant No.5 claiming to be from the News Alert 24 x 7 barged into the shop and making videos of the shop and kitchen wherein sweets were being prepared.

The plaintiff requested the defendant No.5 to show his identity card and he refused to pay any heed and started holding an interview of the henchmen of some paid up men who are not customers of the shop.

The plaintiff submitted that the defendants after leaving the premises yet again over the telephone called for an oral settlement and held the same offer and any failure to comply with the offer, they would screen the doctored images of the kitchen in the press and news channels, ruin the reputation and get the shop permanently shut down.
Hence the present suit.
3. The defendants 1 to 4 after service of summons neither appeared nor contested the suit of the plaintiff.

The defendant No.5 after service of summons appeared through his counsel and filed Written Statement contending that that the defendants 1 to 4 are the local people, regular customer to the plaintiff and they have advised the plaintiff to make clean and maintain hygienic in the place of preparing foods and sweets.
But the plaintiff failed to keep up the promise.

The defendant No.5 submitted that he made oral complaint to the concerned Department to take necessary action against the plaintiff and it was came to the knowledge of the defendants that the officials also hand in glove with the plaintiff and not taken any action against the plaintiff.
The defendants have made inspection of the premises of sweet preparation place, made photograph, taken photos for the purpose of submitting before concerned Department.
The defendant filed a complaint to the Commissioner for Food and Health Controller on 18.2.2022 and also filed complaint before jurisdictional police on 6.2.2022 against the plaintiff.
The defendants 1 to 4 have made the complaint, sought action from the concerned Department.

Since no action taken from the Departments, the defendants with the social obligations for the public and the locality has taken protest and requested the plaintiff to keep up cleanness and hygienic of the place where food is prepared and except this the defendants have no interest in the business of the plaintiff.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the suit with exemplary cost.
4. From the above pleadings this Court has framed with following issues:
(1) Whether the plaintiff proves that he is in prima facie possession of the suit schedule property ?
(2) Whether the plaintiff proves that defendants are causing interference with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit property without having any rights ?

12. The defendant No.1 has not made any attempt to cross-examine the P.W.1 to disprove the oral and documentary evidence.
Therefore, the evidence of P.W.1 is remained undisputed.
Mere filing of written statement is not sufficient to discard the claim made by the plaintiff against defendants including defendant No.5.
The plaintiff by leading oral and documentary evidence proved his claim against the defendants and if the defendants are not restrained, it is very difficult for the plaintiff to run his business.

Admittedly the defendants have no right to obstruct the possession of plaintiff to run the business in the schedule property and if the plaintiff violated the terms of license issued by the concerned Department, it is the look out of the said Department to take action against the plaintiff.
Therefore, the defendants have no right to obstruct the running of plaintiffs business.
In view of above said reason, I hold issues No.1 to 4 in the Affirmative.

13. Issue No. 5 : In view discussions on Issues No.1 to 4, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER Suit of the plaintiff is decreed without cost.
